newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: BLUE CHIPS GAIN AS TURNOVER REVIVES.
newsitem.headline: BLUE CHIPS GAIN AS TURNOVER REVIVES.

text.p: Blue chips gained in healthy turnover on Friday and brokers said some gains had been expected as market players felt prices had fallen too low.
Official list shares jumped 12.30 points to 906.77 points. Group A shares edged down 1.84 points to 1880.99 points.
Market favourites Hermis Bank and Vilniaus Bank led the revival as investors picked up the blue chips on the hope that the time was right for a general increase in shares.

Hermis Bank advanced to 195 litas from 190 litas on central market turnover of about 40,000 litas. Brokers expect it to pass 200 litas, possibly next week. Hermis turned over 475,000 litas in block trades at 190 litas.
Despite showing positive results all year, Hermis shares prices have suffered due to a depressed market.
But brokers note that Hermis, along with Vilniaus, has been one of the first to benefit from new-found optimism.
Vilniaus Bank edged up to 230 litas from 228 litas.
In group A trading, Lithuanian Gas, which heavily weighs down the index, slid to 1.63 litas from 1.65 litas in tiny turnover of 1,170 litas.
Others on the A list faired better. Kalnapilis, which has become a summertime favourite of brokers, rose to 6.20 litas from 6.08 in central market turnover of about 156,000 litas.
Brokers say bargain hunters had been hoping to get the shares at lower prices but finally gave in today.
Klaipeda Stevedoring Company (KLASCO) increased to 12 litas from 11.81 litas on central market turnover of 26,000 litas.
"They gained 20 percent in the last two weeks," said one broker. "They announced good five-month results, better than anyone expected."
